notes: Read all three units, full drug-policy context, all five candidates and the review. Named President Bush in the Access to Recovery account. Replaced the armies-of-compassion metaphor with the faith-based and community organizations it denotes, and restored the omitted assertions about those organizations' local, often congregation-based roots and their leaders' view of disadvantaged people.

claims.claim_text: President Bush's Access to Recovery program was expanding treatment seekers' access to effective providers through a new voucher program.
Government should partner with, rather than rival, faith-based and community organizations serving disadvantaged people.
Faith-based and community organizations serving disadvantaged people are locally rooted and often based in churches, synagogues, mosques and temples.
Leaders of faith-based and community organizations view disadvantaged people as neighbors, friends and moral individuals created in God's image rather than as statistics.
